differential: Pulmonary embolism

Acute heart failure
This can present with sudden shortness of breath, especially in individuals with underlying cardiac risk factors.
Pneumonia
While often more gradual, sudden onset dyspnea can occur with rapidly progressing pneumonia.
Pneumothorax
This can cause sudden shortness of breath due to lung collapse.
Asthma exacerbation
Although less likely with sudden onset in a 58-year-old, it remains a possibility.
Pulmonary embolism
Recent femur fracture and immobility increase the risk of venous thromboembolism leading to sudden cardiac arrest.
Acute myocardial infarction
Sudden cardiac arrest can be caused by an acute blockage of a coronary artery.
Arrhythmia
A sudden, life-threatening arrhythmia can cause cardiac arrest.
Aortic dissection
Although less likely, aortic dissection can present with sudden cardiac arrest.
Tension pneumothorax
While less common, tension pneumothorax can cause sudden cardiac arrest due to impaired venous return.
Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension
The presence of fibrous connective tissue around the pulmonary artery lumen suggests chronic thromboembolic changes.
Pulmonary Embolism
Given the recent femur fracture and immobility, a pulmonary embolism leading to cardiac arrest is a strong possibility.
Pulmonary Artery Sarcoma
Although rare, intimal sarcoma can cause pulmonary artery obstruction and present with similar histological findings.
Primary Pulmonary Hypertension
Fibrous changes in the pulmonary artery could be due to idiopathic pulmonary hypertension.
Pulmonary Veno-Occlusive Disease
This rare condition can cause pulmonary hypertension with histological findings of fibrosis.
eliminated: ARDS is less likely given the specific histological finding of fibrous tissue around the pulmonary artery.

differential: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension

Pulmonary embolism
Although chronic, the initial presentation with sudden shortness of breath and cardiac arrest could be triggered by a new thromboembolic event on top of the chronic disease.
Primary pulmonary hypertension
While less likely given the thrombi, primary pulmonary hypertension can present similarly and should be considered.
Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease
This is a rare cause of pulmonary hypertension that can mimic CTEPH, although the thrombi make it less likely.
Sarcoidosis
Sarcoidosis can cause pulmonary hypertension through granulomatous infiltration of the pulmonary vasculature.
eliminated: The autopsy findings of chronic thrombi and recanalization do not support ARDS.
